rv.q: The best “Uncle Vanya” we’ve seen, it has a lot going for it.
Uncle Vanya brings that feeling front and center and offers understanding through catharsis.
Still, AstonRep’s production suffers from elements misaligned with Chekhov’s intricate and intimate play, out of step with the scale of not just the venue but the text itself.
I have simply no idea what to make of this manic, hyperactive, and grating Vanya other than to say that it is almost spectacular in how misplaced it is.
Delivering a wonderfully feisty and fiery Vanya, Jairell makes the play more than just an avuncular narrative.
Despite its attractive production elements and a few noteworthy performances, this adaptation of Uncle Vanya struggles to capture the emotional depth and complexity that make Chekhov’s work enduring.

cn.t: AstonRep's production of Chekhov's classic receives mixed reviews, with critics divided on the execution. Rian Jairell's performance as Vanya earns praise, though some find the staging uneven and out of tune with the material.
